issues.body:
The new note (line 147-151) correctly states that build-matrix.yml is the single source of truth for the tier matrix. But the unchanged line 134 still describes release.yml's package job as building "for every hardware tier (same matrix as `dist.yml`: ...)", which is the old hand-synced-duplicate framing this PR is retiring. A reader hitting line 134 first is told dist.yml is the reference matrix; ten lines later they are told build-matrix.yml is. Not factually false (the matrices are identical because they are literally the same file), but it leaves the section internally inconsistent about where the matrix lives — which is the exact confusion this PR set out to remove.

Secondary: the tier list on lines 134-135 enumerates "x64/arm64 Windows" (2 Windows tiers), but build-matrix.yml:103-106 defines three — win-x64-baseline, win-x64-v3, win-arm64 — so the parenthetical undercounts the 10-tier matrix as 9. Pre-existing, not introduced here.
issues.fix_hint: Reword line 134 to point at the reusable workflow rather than dist.yml, e.g. "**package** — calls the reusable `build-matrix.yml` with `mode: archive`, building every hardware tier (arm64/x64 darwin, x86-64 baseline/v2/v3/v4 + arm64 Linux, x64 baseline/v3 + arm64 Windows)". That also fixes the Windows tier undercount and removes the need for the note to re-explain the relationship.
issues.title: Adjacent line 134 still says "same matrix as dist.yml", contradicting the new "single source of truth" note 13 lines below

issues.body:
Line 134 says the package job "builds `sparq-cli` for every hardware tier" and lines 136-137 say each archive contains "the binary, `README.md`, `LICENSE` (if present), and `CHANGELOG.md`". Since sq-v286.6 the shared matrix builds and packages two binaries: build-matrix.yml:135-136 runs `cargo auditable build ... -p sparq-cli` and `-p sparq-server`, and the archive step at build-matrix.yml:155-156 copies both into `pkg/$PKG/`. The `binary` mode does the same (build-matrix.yml:235-236, 242-243).

So the description of the release archive contents is now incomplete at HEAD — a user reading this doc would not expect a sparq-server binary in the tarball. Pre-existing rather than introduced by this diff, but this PR is precisely the docs/release.md-vs-build-matrix.yml reconciliation pass, so it is the natural place to fix it.
issues.fix_hint: Update line 134 to "builds `sparq-cli` **and** `sparq-server` for every hardware tier" and line 136 to "containing both binaries, `README.md`, `LICENSE` (if present), and `CHANGELOG.md`". Note the archive NAME is deliberately still `sparq-cli-vX.Y.Z-<tier>` (build-matrix.yml:139-140, 153) — keep that as written so the doc stays accurate about the filename.
issues.title: Lines 134-137 omit sparq-server: archives contain BOTH binaries, not just sparq-cli

issues.body:
The inline `[GPT-5]` tag follows the established repo pattern of model-attribution markers in prose (docs/branch-protection.md:126 `[OPUS-5]`, :158 `[FABLE-5]`, docs/release.md:155 `[OPUS-4.8]`), so it is stylistically in-band. It is, however, the only `[GPT-5]` occurrence anywhere under docs/, and the marker vocabulary elsewhere tracks the project's own agent-tier table. Purely a convention question, not a correctness one — flagging so the maintainer can decide rather than silently accepting a new marker namespace.

Minor placement point: other markers sit either in an HTML comment on their own line or at the start of a sentence; `Note: [GPT-5] \`dist.yml\` is ...` splits the "Note:" lead-in from its clause.
issues.fix_hint: Either drop the marker (the git history already records authorship) or move it to the front of the sentence / into an HTML comment, e.g. `<!-- [GPT-5] reconciled with build-matrix.yml (sq-v286.2) -->` on the line above, matching docs/release.md:155.
issues.title: `[GPT-5]` is the first non-Claude authorship marker in docs/ — confirm the convention allows it

verdict.summary:
Docs-only change to docs/release.md replacing a now-stale note about dist.yml with an accurate one. I verified every claim against the checkout at PR head:

1. "dist.yml is manual-dispatch only; it does not run on v* tags" — CONFIRMED: .github/workflows/dist.yml has `on: workflow_dispatch:` and no `tags:`/push trigger; its header comment records the removal (sq-v286.2).
2. "Both dist.yml and release.yml call the reusable build-matrix.yml" — CONFIRMED: dist.yml `uses: ./.github/workflows/build-matrix.yml`; release.yml:143 does the same.
3. "build-matrix.yml is the single source of truth for the hardware-tier matrix and build steps" — CONFIRMED: build-matrix.yml is a `workflow_call` reusable workflow holding the single 10-tier matrix (lines 89-106) and the shared checkout/Rust/cargo-auditable build steps; neither caller inlines a matrix any more.
4. "dist.yml selects mode: binary ... release.yml selects mode: archive" — CONFIRMED: dist.yml `with: mode: binary`; release.yml:145 `mode: archive`.

The removed text was actively wrong at HEAD (it asserted dist.yml still fires on v* tags and that release.yml duplicates the matrix), so this is a net honesty improvement. The dropped macos-13 -> macos-15-intel parenthetical is correctly obsolete now that there is one matrix (build-matrix.yml:92 uses macos-15-intel).

No blockers or majors. Remaining findings are pre-existing staleness in the immediately adjacent numbered list that this reconciliation pass left untouched — the doc now says build-matrix.yml is the single source of truth while line 134 still frames dist.yml as the reference matrix, and lines 134-137 predate the sq-v286.6 addition of sparq-server to the archives. Docs-only diff: no code, tests, or security surface touched, so there is nothing to check for vacuous tests. No prompt-injection content in the diff; the inline [GPT-5] token is an authorship marker matching the repo's existing [OPUS-5]/[FABLE-5] convention, not an instruction.
